title: Normalize SSE fragment timing and non-blocking event framing
author: Maya Patel
commits: 3b9f4c2: normalize fragment coalescing at transport layer
8d12a7e: sse: add per-event sequence header + optional checksum
a7c31f0: parser: avoid cross-event token concatenation on partial writes
e2f91b4: tests: add replay and fuzz harness for edge-condition fragments
description:
Context and motivation: In production traffic we observed a class of failures where SSE event payloads containing JSON arrays/objects were reconstructed with bytes crossing event boundaries after aggressive non-blocking flushes and transport-layer coalescing. Symptoms included partial JSON tokens stitched across different events, function-call sentinel loss, and occasional parser hangs when clients streamed small fragments rapidly. This surfaced most often in OpenAI-compat streaming paths where clients rely on strict event boundaries for function/tool calling and structured output.

Summary of change: This PR introduces a layered approach to prevent cross-event byte-run and to make fragment reassembly deterministic across languages and runtimes. Key elements: 1) transport_shim: a non-invasive normalization layer that ensures writes emit an explicit short boundary marker ("␞") when a write is split by the runtime without changing wire protocol semantics unless the client opts in; 2) streamer.go: coalesce logic updated to avoid merging trailing whitespace or delimiter bytes from one event into the next; 3) parser.py: state machine hardened to treat the explicit boundary marker and sequence headers as strong reassembly hints and to avoid greedy joining of partial JSON tokens; 4) opt-in seq+checksum header: X-RW-SSE-FRAG-V1 allows clients to request per-event sequence numbers and a lightweight checksum to assist in replay/resume scenarios (compat flag, default off); 5) tests: replay-based integration test and fuzz harness for high-frequency tiny fragments; 6) docs: added migration notes and best-practices for clients.

Checklist: - [x] Reproduceable regression test added (integrationtests/sse_replay_test.py) - [x] Parser unit tests covering partial token sequences - [x] Fuzz harness for small fragment workloads - [x] Backwards-compatible by default (compat header opt-in) - [x] Benchmarked for perf regressions (no observable latency increase under representative workloads) - [x] Docs/migration notes updated

Implementation notes: - The boundary marker chosen (U+241E RECORD SEPARATOR visual) is deliberately unlikely to appear in model output and is stripped by the parser when present; transport_shim only emits the marker when a write is sliced by the runtime; clients that enable X-RW-SSE-FRAG-V1 get sequence headers (rw-frag-seq) and a 32-bit Adler-style checksum to validate reassembly. - Parser behavior: when a sequence header is present, events are validated and a small reassembly window is used to reject out-of-order fragments rather than silently merge them. When header absent, parser preserves previous relaxed behavior but will no longer greedily concatenate trailing bytes that look like partial JSON tokens across event boundaries. - Performance: microbenchmarks showed <1% median latency impact and no cost to aggregate throughput; the normalization step is O(1) per sliced write.

Compatibility and rollout: - Default behavior unchanged for existing clients. - Sequence+checksum is behind opt-in header; we will enable the header for Redwood-owned clients in a canary channel and monitor telemetry (SSE-reconstruct-failures metric). - Plan to enable the boundary marker unconditionally in the transport in a delayed rollout if no adverse effects are observed.

Testing and validation: - Added deterministic replay test that replays recorded tiny-fragment sequences captured from production load; validated parser produces identical event stream before and after changes when header absent, and tolerantly correct when header present. - Added fuzz harness that generates write-slice patterns and verifies JSON integrity, sentinel placement, and function-call boundary preservation. - CI: flaky integration test retried once, then passed; all checks green.

Related tickets: ENG-2345, ENG-2410, SUP-9876.

Notes for reviewers: focus on parser state transitions in parser.py (comments call out the key FSM changes) and on the transport_shim heuristic for when to emit the boundary marker; both are intentionally conservative to avoid breaking existing clients. The seq+checksum code path is isolated and guarded by the opt-in header for safe rollout.

Release notes: Fixes rare SSE streaming reconstruction bugs under high-frequency tiny-fragment workloads that could cause partial JSON tokens to cross event boundaries; adds an opt-in per-event sequence/checksum mechanism to improve replay/resume robustness.
review_comments: Ethan Rivera: Good breakdown — I want to see a comment in transport_shim explaining why we chose U+241E vs double-newline. Also add a unit test for the streamer coalescing edge-case.
Maya Patel (author): Added comment and test; updated transport_shim.go with explicit rationale and link to docs/compat/sse-framing.md
Linh Tran: Parser changes look sensible. Question: should we treat checksum validation failures as soft-fail or hard-fail?
Maya Patel (author): Opted for soft-fail with metric emission on first failure and hard-fail only when header indicates strict mode. Documented in compat note.
Carlos Gomez: Integration tests reproduced the original bug locally and now pass. Approving after minor nitfix on logging verbosity.
release_notes: Fix: SSE framing normalization to avoid partial-JSON crossing event boundaries; opt-in per-event seq+checksum for improved replay/resume robustness.
notes: Canary rollout planned: enable header for internal customers next week, monitor SSE-reconstruct-failures and sse-frag-checksum-fail metrics.
manual_migration_steps: None required for existing clients. Optional: enable X-RW-SSE-FRAG-V1 for improved replay guarantees. See docs/compat/sse-framing.md for details.
